geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the fragmentary split-wing mass with a more continuous profiled section suited to a neighborhood building.
Use a folded section to create one legible upper gesture instead of disconnected block pieces.
Align the sectional gesture with the long axis to reinforce continuity and spatial hierarchy.
Strengthen the public ground response by carving a more explicit access-side void.
Increase void depth so the threshold reads as occupiable public space rather than a shallow subtraction.
Keep the carved void aligned to the access side for an explicit street-facing opening.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing logic with a continuous bent mass to unify the dominant gesture across views.
Keep the bend aligned with the long dimension so the mass reads as one continuous rule rather than fragments.
Tighten the separation to preserve a readable central void without over-fragmenting the mass.
Expand the courtyard slightly so the frontage void becomes a more legible public threshold.
Keep the void opened to the access side so the street relationship remains explicit.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent four-view mass and the parcel/access relationship is present, but the dominant reading is still a boxy split-and-courtyard composition rather than a clear program-shaped neighborhood building. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged by a void/open seam, so the ground response is not sealed, but the form does not yet turn that void into a strong public threshold. The main weakness is section: the silhouette remains mostly repetitive block subtraction, with no compelling roof or inhabited sectional logic to support the requested active neighborhood-living brief. It is plausible as a generic mixed-use mass, but not yet strong enough in program-contract terms to pass hard-fit.

warnings: The form reads as several rectilinear pieces rather than one dominant spatial rule.

Avoid overreading the stepped/cut mass as a resolved section; it is not yet a strong inhabited terrace or roof figure.
